title: Large Language Models for Quantum Code Translation: An Exploratory Study
title_zh: 用于量子代码翻译的大语言模型：一项探索性研究

paragraphs.en: Quantum software development is challenged by quantum-mechanical semantics and fragmented software development kits (SDKs), which complicate cross-SDK code translation and execution. In this paper, we propose an LLM-based approach for translating executable programs between high-level quantum SDKs. We develop a quantum-aware translation workflow whose prompt design and validation reflect quantum semantics and accommodate the version evolution of quantum ecosystems. We conduct a preliminary evaluation of 4 LLM configurations on 43 tasks, translating Qiskit programs to PennyLane and Q#. LLMs achieve a zero-shot Pass@1 of up to 72.33%, while one-shot prompting further improves the translation effectiveness. These results suggest potential for quantum code translation by LLMs.

paragraphs.en: Quantum computing has attracted growing interest, leading to a diverse ecosystem of software development kits (SDKs) and programming languages, including Qiskit [ 10 ] , PennyLane [ 25 ] , and Q# [ 16 ] . However, quantum software development remains challenging because quantum-mechanical abstractions, such as superposition, entanglement, and probabilistic measurement, are unfamiliar to many software engineers. Meanwhile, heterogeneous SDK interfaces and backend-specific execution models require developers to reconcile different application programming interfaces (APIs) and runtime constraints, complicating quantum software development and maintenance.
paragraphs.zh: 量子计算日益受到关注，催生了多样化的软件开发工具包（SDK）和编程语言生态系统，包括 Qiskit [ 10 ] 、PennyLane [ 25 ] 和 Q# [ 16 ] 。 然而，量子软件开发仍然充满挑战，因为叠加、纠缠和概率测量等量子力学抽象概念对许多软件工程师来说并不熟悉。 与此同时，异构的 SDK 接口和特定于后端的执行模型要求开发者协调不同的应用程序编程接口（API）和运行时约束，使量子软件的开发和维护更加复杂。

sents.zh: 与此同时，异构的 SDK 接口和特定于后端的执行模型要求开发者协调不同的应用程序编程接口（API）和运行时约束，使量子软件的开发和维护更加复杂。

paragraphs.en: Code translation [ 2 , 12 ] is a natural software-engineering response to this interoperability problem. For example, a controlled- X X gate can be expressed in Qiskit as qc.cx(a, b) and in Q# as Controlled X([q[a]], q[b]); , where a and b index the control and target qubits, respectively. A practical translator should perform this API mapping while preserving the source program’s intended behavior or code structure. Large language models (LLMs) are promising candidates for this task because they can interpret code and natural-language specifications, generate code in different programming languages, and have supported activities in quantum software engineering, such as code generation [ 9 ] , comment generation [ 27 ] , and static analysis [ 19 ] . Such intuition and observations motivate us to investigate whether LLMs can translate quantum programs across heterogeneous SDKs while preserving their required behavior and structure.
paragraphs.zh: 代码翻译[2, 12]是针对这一互操作性问题的一种自然的软件工程应对方式。 例如，一个受控-X X门在Qiskit中可表示为qc.cx(a, b)，在Q#中可表示为Controlled X([q[a]], q[b]);，其中a和b分别索引控制量子比特和目标量子比特。 一个实用的翻译器应在执行这种API映射的同时，保留源程序预期的行为或代码结构。 大语言模型（LLMs）是这一任务的有力候选，因为它们能够解读代码和自然语言规格说明，生成不同编程语言的代码，并且已在量子软件工程的多项活动中提供支持，例如代码生成[9]、注释生成[27]和静态分析[19]。 这样的直觉和观察促使我们研究：大语言模型能否在跨异构SDK翻译量子程序的同时，保留其所需的行为和结构。

paragraphs.en: To the best of our knowledge, this paper presents the first proposal of LLM-based quantum code translation between high-level SDKs or programming languages to deal with developer-facing quantum programming. We propose a quantum-aware LLM translation workflow from input tasks to translated programs along with the aggregate analysis. In particular, we contribute a prompt-construction method tailored to quantum code translation: it captures quantum-mechanical semantics, such as qubit ordering and the roles of control and target qubits, together with SDK-specific syntax, version constraints, runtime requirements, and task specifications, thereby accommodating the rapid evolution of quantum programming frameworks. We preliminarily evaluate four LLM configurations on 43 benchmark tasks, translating Qiskit programs to PennyLane and Q# and comparing zero-shot with one-shot prompting for two models. The best zero-shot Pass@1 reaches 72.33% on PennyLane and 71.63% on Q#, while one-shot prompting can substantially improve Pass@1 . Furthermore, we find that missing source artifacts and SDK compilation errors dominate zero-shot failures, accounting for 39.2% and 34.9%, respectively. These findings suggest the potential of LLM-based quantum code translation while identifying key barriers for future research.

paragraphs.en: LLM-based translation of classical code. LLMs have been applied to translate classical code across programming languages [ 18 ] . UniTrans uses execution feedback [ 26 ] , InterTrans explores intermediate translation paths [ 15 ] , and AlphaTrans decomposes repositories and combines translation with multiple validation levels [ 11 ] . These advances motivate applying LLMs to quantum code translation, where preserving behavior also requires accounting for relative phase, bit ordering, control and target roles, and probabilistic measurement outcomes.

paragraphs.en: Quantum code migration across versions. Prior work investigates how quantum code can be migrated across SDK versions [ 22 ] , which involves refactoring the original code to accommodate changes in APIs. By contrast, quantum code translation transfers programs across heterogeneous SDKs or programming languages, which requires reconciling different programming abstractions and execution conventions, rather than handling incremental updates within the same SDK.

paragraphs.en: Quantum code transpilation. Transpilation in quantum computing refers to the process of transforming a quantum circuit into an equivalent one that is compatible with the target quantum hardware or simulator. Several works also perform cross-SDK transpilation, such as Siavash et al. suggesting the use of LLMs [ 20 ] and LinguaQuanta leveraging the gate decomposition [ 24 ] . However, quantum code transpilation is rooted in the hardware-oriented conversion in terms of compilers and backends, while our quantum code translation targets the high-level SDKs that could be used by developers to design quantum code.

paragraphs.en: Quantum code generation. Quantum code generation studies use model-driven engineering or LLMs, including (1) model-based generation, like QuanUML [ 8 ] and M2QCode [ 7 ] ; (2) LLM benchmarking studies like Qiskit Code Assistant [ 5 ] , PennyCoder [ 1 ] , QuanBench [ 9 ] , and QuanBench+ [ 21 ] ; and (3) LLM agents such as QPipe [ 23 ] and QAgent [ 6 ] . Compared to code generation, including multi-platform generation for one task [ 7 ] , our translation task converts a given source program into a target program in another SDK or language while preserving functionality and general structure.

paragraphs.en: Figure 1 summarizes the translation workflow. Candidate generation uses the source program and task specification to produce a target program. In parallel, evaluation preparation comprises two blocks. Reference validation checks reference implementations against the tests in versioned native SDK environments. The Evaluation bundle block packages the validated tests and a runtime manifest for subsequent evaluation. The generated program is then executed and checked against this evaluation bundle. Execution results feed into correctness analysis , which distinguishes failures to deliver or execute a candidate from assertion rejections and relates the latter to the properties tested. Aggregate analysis and reporting summarizes these outcomes across tasks, models, and target SDKs (although Q# is a programming language, we use “SDKs” as shorthand for PennyLane and the Q# development environment to improve readability in both the paper and the experimental code).

sents.en: Reference validation checks reference implementations against the tests in versioned native SDK environments.

sents.en: The Evaluation bundle block packages the validated tests and a runtime manifest for subsequent evaluation.
sents.zh: 评测包模块将经过验证的测试和运行时清单打包，用于后续评测。

sents.en: The generated program is then executed and checked against this evaluation bundle.
sents.zh: 随后执行生成的程序，并根据该评测包进行校验。

sents.en: Execution results feed into correctness analysis , which distinguishes failures to deliver or execute a candidate from assertion rejections and relates the latter to the properties tested.

sents.en: Aggregate analysis and reporting summarizes these outcomes across tasks, models, and target SDKs (although Q# is a programming language, we use “SDKs” as shorthand for PennyLane and the Q# development environment to improve readability in both the paper and the experimental code).

paragraphs.en: We propose three research questions (RQs) to investigate zero-shot translation quality across LLMs and target SDKs, the impact of one-shot prompting, and the failure patterns of the translated programs.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出三个研究问题（RQs），以研究跨大语言模型与目标 SDK 的零样本翻译质量、单样本提示的影响，以及翻译后程序的失败模式。

paragraphs.en: RQ1: How does zero-shot quantum code translation performance vary across model configurations and target SDKs?
paragraphs.zh: RQ1：零样本量子代码翻译的性能在不同模型配置和目标 SDK 之间有何差异？

paragraphs.en: RQ2: How do correctness and failure profiles differ between zero-shot and one-shot prompts?
paragraphs.zh: RQ2：零样本提示与单样本提示的正确性和失败特征有何差异？

paragraphs.en: RQ3: What are the main failure categories in LLM-based quantum code translation?
paragraphs.zh: RQ3：基于大语言模型的量子代码翻译中的主要失败类别有哪些？

paragraphs.en: Benchmark. In the absence of a benchmark specifically designed for quantum code translation, we adopt an open-source benchmark from prior work on evaluating LLM-based quantum code generation, whose overall evaluation framework closely aligns with ours. We select QuanBench [ 9 ] , a recent benchmark of moderate size, for our experiments. Since one canonical reference implementation in QuanBench cannot be reliably reproduced to pass the given assertions, we exclude that task and only use 43 of its 44 original tasks, together with companion tests.

paragraphs.en: LLMs. We group the evaluated LLM configurations into closed-source and open-weight models. The former group includes GPT-5.6-sol (GPT) [ 17 ] configured with medium reasoning effort, while the latter incorporates DeepSeek-V4-Pro (Pro) [ 3 ] , DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Flash) [ 4 ] , and GLM-5.2 (GLM) [ 28 ] . All three open-weight models use a temperature of 0.8 and sample-specific random seeds 42–51. GLM uses high reasoning effort. Pro and Flash use high reasoning effort during planning and disable additional reasoning during final code generation. All other model parameters retain their default configurations.

paragraphs.en: Prompt construction. We translate Qiskit 1.4.6 programs to PennyLane 0.45.1 and to Q# using Microsoft’s Quantum Development Kit (QDK) 1.32.0. The zero-shot prompt omits One-shot example in Figure 2 . For one-shot prompting, we select Pro and GLM, the two configurations with the lowest overall zero-shot performance across the target SDKs (Section 4.3 ). Their one-shot prompts include one verified source–target translation example for the target SDK. In detail, we select a basic task from Qolumbina [ 13 ] , a recent benchmark infrastructure of scalable quantum programs, and manually implement semantically equivalent three-qubit programs for this task in Qiskit, PennyLane, and Q#; this choice is intended to reduce the risk of data leakage. We choose simple examples that do not duplicate the full functionality of any evaluated task, and these examples cover reversible comparisons, conditional bit flips, and phase marking.
paragraphs.zh: 提示词构建。 我们将 Qiskit 1.4.6 程序翻译为 PennyLane 0.45.1 程序，以及使用 Microsoft 的 Quantum Development Kit (QDK) 1.32.0 翻译为 Q# 程序。 图 2 中的零样本提示词省略了单样本示例。 对于单样本提示，我们选择 Pro 和 GLM，这两个配置在目标 SDK 上的整体零样本性能最低（第 4.3 节）。 它们的单样本提示包含一个针对目标 SDK 的经过验证的源-目标翻译示例。 具体而言，我们从 Qolumbina [13]（一个最近提出的可扩展量子程序基准测试基础设施）中选取一个基础任务，并在 Qiskit、PennyLane 和 Q# 中手动实现语义等价的三量子比特程序；这一选择旨在降低数据泄露的风险。 我们选择不重复任何被评估任务的完整功能的简单示例，这些示例涵盖可逆比较、条件比特翻转和相位标记。

paragraphs.en: Evaluation metrics. (1) Effectiveness : Following QuanBench [ 9 ] , we use Pass@ k k to measure the task-macro correctness of the translated programs, where a single task succeeds if it passes all assertions provided by QuanBench. For each task, we have n t n_{t} sample slots (planned translation attempts), among which c t c_{t} are successful. Let 𝒯 \mathcal{T} be the set of retained tasks. The metric is defined as Pass@ k = 1 | 𝒯 | ​ ∑ t ∈ 𝒯 [ 1 − ( n t − c t k ) / ( n t k ) ] . \mbox{Pass@$k$}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{T}|}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\left[1-{\binom{n_{t}-c_{t}}{k}}/{\binom{n_{t}}{k}}\right]. In our experiments, we evaluate k ∈ { 1 , 3 } k\in\{1,3\} using n t = 10 n_{t}=10 sample slots for each model–task–target combination. (2) Cost : We also record the average runtime and output token count per API response to measure the cost of translation.

paragraphs.en: Across the evaluated zero-shot model–target pairs in Table 1 , Pass@1 ranges from 16.28% to 72.33%, indicating substantial variation in translation success: Flash achieves the highest score on PennyLane, while Pro has the lowest on Q#. The ranking also depends on the target SDK: Flash leads on PennyLane, whereas GPT leads on Q#. Target effects vary by model as well: GPT performs better on Q# than on PennyLane, while GLM, Pro, and Flash perform better on PennyLane. In addition, Pass@3 exceeds Pass@1 for every model–target pair, showing that multi-sample evaluation can find passing candidates missed by a single sample. paragraphs.en: We compare Pro and GLM under the zero-shot and one-shot prompt conditions defined in Section 4.2 , using the same task scope and native evaluation bundle. paragraphs.en: Our study presents an initial proposal and a pilot evaluation of LLM-based quantum code translation, with four LLM configurations, two translation targets (PennyLane and Q#), 43 benchmark tasks, and a comparison between zero-shot and one-shot prompts. The results show substantial variation in translation quality across the evaluated LLM configurations and target SDKs, with zero-shot Pass@1 ranging from 16.28% to 72.33%. The most common failure category is missing source, followed by SDK compilation.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究提出了基于大语言模型（LLM）的量子代码翻译的初步方案和试点评估，涉及四种LLM配置、两个翻译目标（PennyLane和Q#）、43个基准任务，以及零样本（zero-shot）与单样本（one-shot）提示之间的比较。 结果表明，在所评估的LLM配置和目标软件开发工具包（SDK）之间，翻译质量存在显著差异，零样本Pass@1的成功率从16.28%到72.33%不等。 最常见的失败类别是缺少源文件，其次是SDK编译失败。

paragraphs.en: In future work, we plan to build a dedicated cross-SDK translation benchmark by integrating existing quantum programs, including scalable programs such as Qolumbina [ 13 ] , with paired source–target implementations and executable tests across SDKs and program sizes. We will also develop translation-specific metrics and assertions for semantic preservation and required structural consistency, drawing on quantum software testing [ 14 ] . These checks will cover relative phase, bit ordering, and probabilistic outputs to complement output-based evaluation. Finally, we will conduct broader empirical studies of prompting strategies and explore execution-guided repair while assessing translation quality and cost.
paragraphs.zh: 在未来的工作中，我们计划通过整合现有的量子程序（包括可扩展程序如 Qolumbina [13]）来构建一个专门的跨 SDK 翻译基准，这些程序具有配对的源—目标实现以及可在不同 SDK 和程序规模上运行的可执行测试。 我们还将借鉴量子软件测试 [14]，开发针对翻译的度量标准和断言，用于评估语义保持性和所需的结构一致性。 这些检查将涵盖相对相位、比特排序以及概率性输出，以补充基于输出的评估。 最后，我们将对提示策略开展更广泛的实证研究，并在评估翻译质量与成本的同时探索执行引导的修复方法。
